Month in brief

Intune plans iOS/iPadOS 18 and macOS 15 floors as DDM guidance expands

August’s 1,727 records were dominated by Configuration Manager, including many metadata-only recategorizations, but the main administrator-facing changes were Intune’s planned Apple OS support updates, new Apple DDM App Settings guidance, and the September 2609 switch to the new single-device page. Firewall guidance also clarified a significant MDM reporting limitation. Other substantive additions covered TPM-backed Windows Autopilot device association and unattended Remote Help for Windows and Android. Configuration Manager’s most consequential exception was a security update requiring a site reset and manual secondary-site recovery.

  • Intune · App management
    Intune plans an iOS/iPadOS 18 minimum after Apple’s 27 release

    Microsoft’s Message Center plan says Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or later after Apple releases iOS/iPadOS 27 later this year. The notice calls for compatibility and Intune-report review and identifies separate OS requirements for userless devices enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment.

  • Intune · Device enrollment
    Intune support moves to macOS 15 and later after Golden Gate 27

    After macOS Golden Gate 27 releases, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Existing devices on macOS 14.x or below remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions won’t be allowed.

  • Intune · Apple
    Apple DDM guidance details supervised app and binary controls

    The new Intune page documents Apple DDM App Settings in the Settings catalog for supervised iOS/iPadOS 27+ and macOS 27+ devices, including allowed or denied apps, binaries, and managed-app allowances. Existing iOS app-launch restrictions in the Restrictions profile must be migrated because iOS 27 deprecates those settings.

  • Intune · Device security
    MDM Firewall and ASR policies provide policy-level reporting only

    Updated Firewall guidance says per-setting reporting is available for most Endpoint Security policies, but Firewall Rules and Attack Surface Reduction Rules managed through MDM report only policy-level status. Per-setting status requires devices enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management.

  • Intune · Endpoint analytics
    The new Intune single-device page becomes default in September 2609

    The new consolidated device-management page will become the default view in the September 2609 release and replace the legacy page. All management features remain, but administrators should update internal documentation and familiarize support teams with the new interface.

For Intune administrators

Inventory Apple device versions and plan upgrades before the support changes; also check the separate OS requirements called out for userless devices enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment. For Apple DDM App Settings, use the Settings catalog on supported supervised devices and migrate iOS Restrictions-profile app-launch settings deprecated by iOS 27. Set reporting expectations for MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules: per-setting status requires devices enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management. Update runbooks for the September 2609 device-page change. Configuration Manager teams on versions 2603, 2509, or 2503 with the required rollups should plan the site reset and secondary-site recovery. Use operatingSystemVersion for new assignment filters; existing‌

This period briefing was generated by AI from the tracked Microsoft Learn and Message Center changes.
